extracted.intended_audience: Personnel assigned or designated to perform public information duties during an incident, emergency, or disaster; any responder who may be assigned public information duties.
extracted.subtask_description: A four-day, 32-contact-hour training course for current or potential Public Information Officers that teaches NIMS/ICS integration, message development/delivery, Joint Information Center operations, legal considerations, and practical exercises in emergency public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Public Information Officer and the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrate the multiple roles of the Public Information Officer and the media in planning for and responding to an emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical knowledge of the role of the Public Information Officer is taught so students understand how PIOs and media interact in both planning and response phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal aspects associated with emergencies and public information
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize various legal aspects associated with emergencies and public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction includes legal considerations that affect what information can be released and how to manage legal constraints during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand NIMS and ICS correlation with emergency response
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the National Incident Management System, Incident Command System and their correlation with the emergency response system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course ties public information roles and JIC operations into NIMS/ICS structures so students can operate within the broader incident management framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct and deliver crisis and emergency risk messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct and deliver an appropriate crisis and emergency risk message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers message development and delivery, risk communication principles, and how to tailor messages for crisis contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather, verify, coordinate, and disseminate public information from a JIC
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather, verify, coordinate, and disseminate public information in an emergency from a Joint Information Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students practice JIC functions including information collection, verification and coordinated dissemination through exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency communications methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical knowledge of emergency communications methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes instruction on communication channels and techniques appropriate to incident/emergency contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk communication skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training focuses on principles of communicating risk to the public clearly and effectively during emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpersonal skills for public information work
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpersonal skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes interpersonal skills necessary for coordinating with responders, the public, and media under stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message development and delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Message development and delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students learn how to develop clear, actionable messages and how to deliver them via press conferences and other outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press conferences and media interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Press conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course includes practical exercises in conducting press conferences and interacting with media representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation of a Joint Information Center (JIC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of a Joint Information Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers JIC structure, functions, and how to integrate public information activities within a JIC environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stress management for PIOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Stress management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides strategies for managing stress while performing public information duties during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic communication and planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic communication and planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students learn to create strategic communication plans to guide messaging and operations during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical activities: writing messages and conducting press conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Students conduct various public information activities and exercises, to include writing messages and conducting press conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-on exercises are used to practice message writing and media engagement skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capstone practical exercise: plan, develop, integrate, and disseminate public information
rubrics_metrics.description: Course culminates with a practical exercise designed to plan, develop, integrate, and disseminate public information for an emergency, incident, or disaster as part of a Joint Information Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final exercise evaluates students' ability to apply course concepts in a simulated JIC environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel who are assigned or may be designated to perform public information duties during an incident, emergency, or disaster and anyone in a response discipline who may be assigned or designated to perform public information duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies intended student population so course content is tailored to active or potential PIOs and other responders with PIO responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite course requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the course, the student must successfully complete the following courses: IS-100.b (or IS-100/ICS-100 series), IS-200.b (or IS-200/ICS-200 series), and IS-700.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful completion of these foundational ICS/NIMS courses is mandatory before attending MPI MGT-902.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended preparatory courses
rubrics_metrics.description: The completion of the following courses is recommended but not required: ICS-300 (IS-300), ICS-400 (IS-400), IS-702.a (NIMS Public Information Systems), and IS-800.c (National Response Framework).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These advanced/reinforcing courses are suggested to better prepare students for course content and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course length and contact hours
rubrics_metrics.description: MPI is a four-day course that provides 32 Contact Hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistical requirement indicating time commitment and course intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Education Credits (IACET)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center for Domestic Preparedness is an Accredited Provider of Continuing Education Units (CEU) and is authorized to award IACET – 3.2 CEUs for successful completion of this activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates professional credit awarded upon successful course completion.
